To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel asynchronous multiuser deep RL framework for handover control in possibly large-scale systems, where the UEs with different mobility patterns are clustered and the asynchronous framework enables the training of the DNN-based controllers to be faster with more UES.

we propose a two-level framework to learn the handover (HO)-based mobility management scheme in wireless systems, where we use asynchronous multiuser deep RL to learn the HO processes across different users with heterogeneous mobility patterns in each cluster, and the global-parameter-based asynchronous multiuser framework can be trained faster with more users, which is suitable for the scalability issue in large systems.

(i) We develop a two-layer framework for handover (HO), where the user equipments (Ues) are partitioned into clusters based on their mobility patterns, which can be heterogeneous; and (ii) We develop a multiuser deep reinforcement-learning (RL) scheme for each cluster, where each UE learns a DNN controller in a collaborative fashion, and we also use supervised learning to mitigate the negative effect of random exploration at initialization.

the development of an asynchronous multiuser DRL framework to support the handover control in possibly large-scale heterogeneous wireless systems, which is of high practical relevance.

the design of a two-layer framework for handover control in possibly large-scale heterogeneous wireless systems.
